newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares close mixed in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares close mixed in cautious trade.

text.p: Trading was mixed on Thursday on the Nigerian stock market amid continuing investor caution, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 6621.18, up from 6616.17 on Wednesday.
But blue chips Lever Brothers and Nigerian Breweries dropped further as investors continued to sell their shares.
Lever Brothers fell five kobo for the second day running to 25.55 naira.
Nigerian Breweries slid 10 kobo to 11.20 naira, while Guinness was unchanged at 7.30 naira.
UAC was 15 kobo lower at 9.65 naira while John Holt lost one kobo at 10.39 naira.
An improved third quarter profit posted by construction firm Costain West Africa boosted its shares four kobo to 1.81 naira.
But Seven-Up Bottling Company's equally improved half year result got a cold reception, closing unchanged at 1.36 naira.
Other food shares were higher, with Nestle up 30 kobo to 36.80 naira, Union Dicon Salt up six at 36.72 and National Salt Company rose four to 4.88 naira.
Cement Company of Northern Nigeria which announced lower six-month profit to end-June lost five kobo to 3.00 naira while Benue Cement went ex-dividend at 7.37 naira, down 15 kobo.

Petroleum marketing shares were stronger. Agip led the pack, rising 30 kobo to 15.50 naira. Mobil and Total were 20 kobo up, to 41.30 naira and 48.80 naira respectively, while Unipetrol rose 15 kobo to 43.50 naira.
